title: 美债收益率19年高：美联储为何不动，加息信号被无视
speaker: Bloomberg

segments.en: It's very clear that bond yields at 19-year high send us something, it's a warning signal for Kevin Worsh at the Fed, does that challenge his expectations?
segments.zh: 19年高位的债券收益率显然在发出警告信号，这对美联储的Kevin Worsh意味着什么？会挑战他的预期吗？

segments.en: So I think it was a real surprise, I think a lot of people were expecting him to come out and give us strong performance at the press conference and fairly or unfairly the market
segments.zh: 我认为这确实令人意外，很多人期待他在新闻发布会上有强劲表现，但无论公平与否，市场

segments.en: has sort of judged this as a weaker press conference than expected.
segments.zh: 认为这次发布会比预期要弱。

segments.en: And I think principally because there was an air gap between the rhetoric around commitment to price stability and awareness that inflation has been away from the 2% target in the
segments.zh: 主要是因为关于价格稳定的承诺与对通胀偏离2%目标的认识之间存在脱节，

segments.en: US for really quite a long time, five years, and yet not taking, looking like there was no appetite to surprise markets with what is not a very dramatic 25 basis point hike.
segments.zh: 美国通胀偏离目标已长达五年，但似乎没有意愿通过加息25个基点来给市场带来意外。

segments.en: Now a charitable view of that would be that perhaps he's finding his feet a little bit like President Lagarde in the early days you may recall, and now she's seen this quite
segments.zh: 从善意的角度看，他可能像早期的拉加德行长一样在摸索，而她现在已成为一位出色的央行行长。

segments.en: incredible central banker, so I think clearly all is no lost, that perhaps he's falling more in the footsteps of an incremental approach despite what he was talking about at the press
segments.zh: 所以显然并非全无希望，他可能更倾向于渐进式做法，尽管他在发布会上谈论的是另一回事。
